questions.question: Use a TRANSITION when you want to:

options.text: Smoothly interpolate a property change between two states
Run a multi-step keyframe loop automatically

questions.explanation: Transitions are for state-to-state tweens (hover, toggle). Animations are for keyframe sequences.

questions.question: Use an ANIMATION when you need:

options.text: Multiple keyframe steps, looping, or auto-running on load

questions.explanation: Animations handle sequences, iteration-count, direction, and auto-start — beyond what a transition offers.

questions.question: A transition requires a:
questions.explanation: Transitions are passive — they fire only when a watched property actually changes value.

questions.question: Which can loop infinitely without JS?
questions.explanation: Only keyframe animations support looping/auto-run; transitions always interpolate a single change.

questions.question: Both animations and transitions can be interrupted/reversed by:

options.text: Changing the property again (e.g. removing :hover) — the browser tweens to the new state

questions.explanation: Both are interruptible; reversing the condition smoothly returns to the prior state if transition/timing is defined.

questions.question: Performance-wise, both are fine when animating:
questions.explanation: Whichever you pick, prefer transform/opacity to avoid layout thrash and jank.

questions.question: A loading spinner is best done with:
questions.explanation: Continuous rotation needs a looping keyframe animation (transform: rotate), not a one-shot transition.

questions.question: A button hover color change is best done with:
questions.explanation: A hover color/opacity shift is exactly what transitions are for — no keyframes needed.
